event.summary: Check first recipe-build ownership against concurrent place retarget/removal
event.detail: Reviewed commit: 56659839785691f76da3af5d8f51b511cff4ba8b. TLDR: A first recipe image build may race removal or retargeting of its container host before durable resource ownership becomes visible. Source basis: new refuse_referenced_place checks only existing row and RecipeState.needs_cleanup facts (store/podman.rs:215-249); rebuild admission probes its place before prepare_images, whose first edit only clears last_failure (environment/podman.rs:937; environment/podman/build.rs:246-263). Need inspect helper ownership publication and current route checks to determine whether a started command can still be aimed at an old endpoint or lose cleanup access. Contract: SPEC_impl.md Environment rows and provider state refuses removal/retarget while recipe state records artifacts, retaining access for confirmed cleanup. Suggested bucket: other or high if route loss is established; could-be-highest: not established, possible stranded helper processes require tracing. Confidence: uninvestigated lead; no execution. proposed_drop: false. possible_cover: none. Next checks: helper and edit transactions, place resolution and endpoint guards, plus retarget/removal callers.

event.summary: First helper ownership is serialized with place removal and retarget
event.detail: Reviewed commit: 56659839785691f76da3af5d8f51b511cff4ba8b. TLDR of considered consequence: A first recipe build could strand a helper at an old or forgotten container host if ownership publication raced host removal/retarget. Source checks refute that route. environment/podman/build.rs:538-565 calls edit_at with the HostRow paired with the observed route before run; edit_at at 488-500 calls update_recipe_place_state. tensorlake/build.rs:330-340 uses an immediate transaction to recheck kind, entry UUID and destination; it records ownership in the same transaction at 342-364. A winning removal/retarget makes that write fail; a winning ownership write makes the new refuse_referenced_place at store/podman.rs:226-249 reject removal/retarget through needs_cleanup (environment/recipes.rs:66-74). environment/podman.rs:150-184 resolves and checks the current route again per operation. A preceding base-image pull is user-base storage rather than a launched owned helper. Contract: SPEC_impl.md Environment rows and provider state says removal/retarget is refused while recipe state records artifacts, retaining the cleanup route. Suggested bucket if established: high for lost cleanup access; could-be-highest: the suspected stranded-process consequence was considered, but no shipped route survives the transaction guard. Confidence: confirmed source refutation; no execution. proposed_drop: source-refuted by the guarded ownership transaction and existing-refusal transaction. possible_cover: none. No unresolved premise remains for this lead.

event.summary: Post-publication cleanup guard does not establish pre-publication consent
event.detail: Reviewed commit: 56659839785691f76da3af5d8f51b511cff4ba8b. TLDR of original considered consequence: a first recipe build could strand a helper at an old or forgotten container host if ownership publication raced removal/retarget. The prior source-refuted proposed drop is preserved ONLY for that cleanup race after helper ownership is transactionally admitted. environment/podman/build.rs:538-565 writes helper intent through edit_at before run; tensorlake/build.rs:330-364 validates current kind, entry UUID and destination with state publication in one immediate transaction. store/podman.rs:215-249 then refuses endpoint loss. This starts at ownership publication; pending approval cards are not references checked here. It does not bind an earlier card to the physical endpoint it named. g020/l1 (reviewed 190d844e58c96cf197aa838d0b0eea8062f48435) now reports a separate pre-publication route: first container at an ordinary SSH place without retained rows/images/helpers, a requester on a different ordinary host, destination retarget plus fresh probe while its card waits, and later execution/credential delivery on the replacement endpoint. That reported highest consequence is NOT refuted by this candidate. Need independently check the exact admission boundary against that later caller; no new duplicate finding asserted yet. Original suggested bucket if stranded-helper consequence were established: high, with could-be-highest for lost processes considered but source-refuted in the original transactional route. Confidence: confirmed post-publication guard, pre-publication cross-group premise to verify. proposed_drop: retain source refutation of original cleanup race only; do not drop the distinct stale-consent route. possible_cover: g020/l1 owns the pre-publication approval finding. event.summary: Cleanup ownership fence starts after the earlier approval boundary
event.detail:
# Cleanup ownership fence starts after the earlier approval boundary

Reviewed commit: 56659839785691f76da3af5d8f51b511cff4ba8b; cross-group approval caller independently checked at 190d844e58c96cf197aa838d0b0eea8062f48435.

## TLDR

The original suspected loss of cleanup access from retargeting after a helper is recorded is source-refuted. That guard does not protect the machine named by a pending approval before anything is registered. The distinct stale approval can deliver execution and recipe credentials to a retargeted machine; g020/l1 owns that finding.

## Details

Original consequence preserved: a first recipe build could strand a helper at an old or forgotten host if ownership publication raced removal/retarget. The initial proposed drop remains valid for that precise race. environment/podman/build.rs:538-565 publishes helper intent through edit_at before run; edit_at:488-500 calls update_recipe_place_state. tensorlake/build.rs:330-364 rechecks kind, entry UUID and destination in an immediate transaction with ownership publication. A winning endpoint mutation refuses stale helper publication; a winning publication sets needs_cleanup, making store/podman.rs:226-249 refuse retarget/removal in their own transaction. A preceding pull holds only a user-base image rather than an owned running helper. Original suggested bucket if established: high for lost cleanup access; could-be-highest for lost owned processes was considered but that route is refuted. No original consequence is withdrawn merely for rarity.

The exact fence begins when a hosts.place_host reference is inserted or recipe state starts needing cleanup. It is not admission for a pre-existing card. At the later approval revision, agent_requests.rs:4485-4515 captures place_name and numeric Place then waits for approval, with no resource registration or target destination/connection snapshot. approved:2865-2886 rechecks the requesting origin only. After Allow, agent_requests.rs:4541-4549 calls start_session_environment with that numeric place. provisioning/tensorlake_add.rs:379-398 checks CURRENT availability and registers ownership; store/podman.rs:364-394 reads CURRENT host kind and inserts the first row without an expected endpoint parameter. A cold place with no rows or resource state passes refuse_referenced_place:215-250 throughout the earlier card wait. A requester on another ordinary host is unaffected by a change to this separate container place. The later fresh probe is tied to the new current endpoint (podman_probe.rs:304-332,383-404), and Podman commands resolve that endpoint (podman.rs:150-184); those compare against a new probe, never the old card. Delivery resolves the environment's current route (credential_delivery.rs:434-440) and installs Codex auth.json (603-608) or a configured GitHub token (631-652). Thus the post-publication cleanup guard cannot refute g020/l1's earlier authority-substitution premise. The original source refutation never established that earlier consent boundary.

Exact separate approval contract at 190d844e58c96cf197aa838d0b0eea8062f48435, SPEC_impl.md:9548-9556: 'What a card shows is what an approval does.' and 'A launch is also refused if the target host’s connection changed while the card waited, since the approval was for the machine the card named.' (The source uses an ASCII apostrophe in host's.) This is independent from SPEC_impl.md Environment rows and provider state's requirement to retain cleanup access once resource ownership exists.

Suggested bucket for the separate g020 route: highest because the shipped credential-copy route is established; its trigger requires a cold ordinary SSH place, concurrent operator retarget and a usable fresh probe, with requester on a different ordinary host. Confidence: confirmed source boundary and concrete credential delivery; no runtime observation. could-be-highest: yes for the separate consent finding, not refuted or lowered here. proposed_drop: retain original source-refuted no-report decision ONLY for the post-publication lost-cleanup race. No drop is proposed for the pre-publication approval issue. possible_cover: g020/l1 is the existing finding for that issue; this candidate records the independent store-boundary result without creating a duplicate queue item. No unresolved readily checkable premise remains in this assigned boundary analysis.

event.summary: Integrated container ownership keeps the accepted WAL power-loss limit
event.detail:
# Integrated container ownership keeps the accepted WAL power-loss limit

Reviewed commit: 56659839785691f76da3af5d8f51b511cff4ba8b

## TLDR

An OS crash or power loss on the helm machine can lose recently committed container ownership or create facts even though a remote container survives. This can require explicit leftover cleanup or manual recovery of running work. This is a real integrated creation route, not the foundation revision's missing-caller case, but the specification explicitly accepts ordinary WAL tail loss.

## Details

register_container uses self.conn.call and commits registration at store/podman.rs:373-394. set_podman_prepared_create atomically writes login, selected install facts and pending send with self.conn.call at 268-278. environment/podman.rs:1103-1125 awaits that write before sending run. Canonical ID observation uses the same ordinary call at store/podman.rs:422-432; installation admission does too at 315-329. Db::call only locks and runs work (farhelm-supervisor/src/db.rs:230-245); it does not upgrade durability. configure_durability sets NORMAL when actual mode is WAL (db.rs:94-117). The separate FULL/EXTRA helper is invoked only explicitly (db.rs:247-266). The integrated provisioning caller registers before preparation (provisioning/tensorlake_add.rs:388-408), creates before reading saved facts/admitting paths (555-594), then delivers credentials (597-605), attaches, and creates the session in finish_session_launch (981-1013). No mandatory full-sync barrier is supplied by these ownership APIs before external create. A remote place can remain alive when only the helm machine loses power. This establishes potential loss of the registry/marker association, not database corruption or automatic destruction of the remote files.

Recovery is conservative: decode_binding requires complete login for created/admitted rows (store/podman.rs:148-165); create adopts a name only with recorded canonical or pending identity (environment/podman.rs:1071-1093), otherwise it refuses the collision. destroy returns never-created when both ID and pending marker are absent (1298-1302), so loss of those records cannot by itself authorize deleting the surviving resource. Normal initial-launch failure explicitly cleans only its new environment (provisioning/tensorlake_add.rs:1028-1044); a power failure does not resume this task at startup. Label-based leftovers are listed at usable places and places referenced by rows or recipe artifacts (environment/podman.rs:771-835), with rowless explicit deletion ownership-checked at 725-765. Thus tail loss can strand work from its normal UI association and require manual recovery, but available source does not establish irreversible loss of the files/processes themselves. A helm process crash alone preserves committed ownership under the stated contract.

Exact specification acceptance, SPEC_impl.md Helm internals:5668-5672: 'Its ordinary store opens share the supervisor’s journal setup: owning opens attempt WAL before migrations, warning and continuing in the current mode if conversion fails or does not return `wal`. Non-owning opens never convert; every ordinary read-write connection selects `synchronous=NORMAL` only after reading an actual WAL mode and otherwise retains FULL. This accepts losing the last commits on an OS crash or power loss without weakening database consistency; process crashes preserve commits.' Same contract at 6683-6685 explicitly says: 'A legacy row or a power loss that lost both records cannot recover by name: remove that host entry, then handle the leftover explicitly.' Snapshot-build ownership at 6840-6841 says: 'Ordinary write durability is retained: a legacy row or power loss that loses both the ID and pending marker requires explicit cleanup.' The Podman integration continues ordinary store durability rather than introducing a listed trust-revocation exception.

Suggested bucket: high for the source-established lost normal access/cleanup association if reported; could-be-highest: yes, the original potential loss of user work/processes is preserved for independent checking, but no shipped irreversible-loss or silent-destructive-recovery route was established. Confidence: confirmed source and contract analysis of the write policy/caller; no execution or reproduction and no claim that a particular crash was observed to lose a commit. proposed_drop: exact explicit specification acceptance of ordinary WAL power-loss tail loss and explicit cleanup above, NOT missing integrated caller. Retain as a finding with proposed_drop for the independent check because the original concern could be highest. possible_cover: g064/c3 examines the foundation/endpoint scope; this record supplies the integrated assigned-store caller and recovery analysis. No readily checkable missing premise remains for this conclusion.

This can require explicit leftover cleanup or manual recovery of running work. This is a real integrated creation route, not the foundation revision's missing-caller case, but the specification explicitly accepts ordinary WAL tail loss.

## Details

register_container uses self.conn.call and commits registration at store/podman.rs:373-394. set_podman_prepared_create atomically writes login, selected install facts and pending send with self.conn.call at 268-278. environment/podman.rs:1103-1125 awaits that write before sending run. Canonical ID observation uses the same ordinary call at store/podman.rs:422-432; installation admission does too at 315-329. Db::call only locks and runs work (farhelm-supervisor/src/db.rs:230-245); it does not upgrade durability. configure_durability sets NORMAL when actual mode is WAL (db.rs:94-117). The separate FULL/EXTRA helper is invoked only explicitly (db.rs:247-266). The integrated provisioning caller registers before preparation (provisioning/tensorlake_add.rs:388-408), creates before reading saved facts/admitting paths (555-594), then delivers credentials (597-605), attaches, and creates the session in finish_session_launch (981-1013). No mandatory full-sync barrier is supplied by these ownership APIs before external create. A remote place can remain alive when only the helm machine loses power. This establishes potential loss of the registry/marker association, not database corruption or automatic destruction of the remote files.

Recovery is conservative: decode_binding requires complete login for created/admitted rows (store/podman.rs:148-165); create adopts a name only with recorded canonical or pending identity (environment/podman.rs:1071-1093), otherwise it refuses the collision. destroy returns never-created when both ID and pending marker are absent (1298-1302), so loss of those records cannot by itself authorize deleting the surviving resource. Normal initial-launch failure explicitly cleans only its new environment (provisioning/tensorlake_add.rs:1028-1044); a power failure does not resume this task at startup. Label-based leftovers are listed at usable places and places referenced by rows or recipe artifacts (environment/podman.rs:771-835), with rowless explicit deletion ownership-checked at 725-765. Thus tail loss can strand work from its normal UI association and require manual recovery, but available source does not establish irreversible loss of the files/processes themselves. A helm process crash alone preserves committed ownership under the stated contract.

Exact specification acceptance, SPEC_impl.md Helm internals:5668-5672: 'Its ordinary store opens share the supervisor's journal setup: owning opens attempt WAL before migrations, warning and continuing in the current mode if conversion fails or does not return `wal`. Non-owning opens never convert; every ordinary read-write connection selects `synchronous=NORMAL` only after reading an actual WAL mode and otherwise retains FULL. This accepts losing the last commits on an OS crash or power loss without weakening database consistency; process crashes preserve commits.' Same contract at 6683-6685 explicitly says: 'A legacy row or a power loss that lost both records cannot recover by name: remove that host entry, then handle the leftover explicitly.' Snapshot-build ownership at 6840-6841 says: 'Ordinary write durability is retained: a legacy row or power loss that loses both the ID and pending marker requires explicit cleanup.' The Podman integration continues ordinary store durability rather than introducing a listed trust-revocation exception.

Suggested bucket: high for the source-established lost normal access/cleanup association if reported; could-be-highest: yes, the original potential loss of user work/processes is preserved for independent checking, but no shipped irreversible-loss or silent-destructive-recovery route was established. Confidence: confirmed source and contract analysis of the write policy/caller; no execution or reproduction and no claim that a particular crash was observed to lose a commit. proposed_drop: exact explicit specification acceptance of ordinary WAL power-loss tail loss and explicit cleanup above, NOT missing integrated caller. Retain as a finding with proposed_drop for the independent check because the original concern could be highest. possible_cover: g064/c3 examines the foundation/endpoint scope; this record supplies the integrated assigned-store caller and recovery analysis. No readily checkable missing premise remains for this conclusion.

# Refused-create timestamp comparison has no out-of-order production caller

Reviewed commit: 56659839785691f76da3af5d8f51b511cff4ba8b

## TLDR

Considered whether a delayed refusal could clear a newer container-create marker because send timestamps have only one-second resolution. Source checks establish that the production caller serializes the full create/refusal episode for this environment; no overlapping old result can settle a newer episode through this path. No user-visible defect is established.

## Details

clear_refused_podman_create uses entry UUID, binding coordinates, no canonical ID/admitted paths, and equality on sent at store/podman.rs:450-463. The timestamp is not a unique generation by itself. The only production caller is environment/podman.rs:1135-1145, inside create after awaiting run and a subsequent absent inspection; it clears only a typed CreateRefused. It does not spawn an independent settlement task. Source searches for the setter and clearer at this revision found only this production create implementation plus the changed store test. start_session_environment acquires the environment host's provisioning lock at provisioning/tensorlake_add.rs:452 before spawning the task, and moves the held guard through environment_session_steps into finish_session_launch at 472-484. create is awaited at 555 and completion/cleanup finishes under that same owned guard. Concurrent ordinary deletion is serialized by the same resource admission already checked in the prior synthesis. Thus equal second-level timestamps are not sufficient to create the hypothesized old/new overlapping result route. The new test's stale no-login guard is correctly rejected because the recorded login/marker no longer matches (store/podman.rs:526-531); it does not claim to exercise concurrent delayed command results.

Contract: SPEC_impl.md Disposable environments records observed login, prepared facts and pending-send together before creation; the store's per-create settlement comment at 435-438 describes the caller's serialized episode, not independent concurrent sends. Suggested bucket if stale ownership settlement were reachable: high for losing the automatic cleanup association; could-be-highest: yes in the original hypothetical if loss of that association led to lost user processes/work, but no such production out-of-order route is established. Confidence: confirmed source refutation, not runtime execution. proposed_drop: source-refuted by the sole production caller's awaited settlement and full-episode per-environment provisioning lock; no parent acceptance presumed. possible_cover: none. No unresolved source premise remains; this does not claim that timestamps alone are unique or that arbitrary unsynchronized private-store calls would have a stronger contract.
